To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) an imbalanced tree can be constructed for sequential data broadcasting with skewed data access; (ii) the cost of index probing can be minimized by exploiting the data access skew; (iii) the index fanout can be varied to further reduce the cost of index probe.

the cost of indexed sequential data broadcast can be minimized not by using a balanced index tree but by using an unbalanced one, and that the cost can be further minimized by exploiting variant fanout sizes for index nodes.
the proposed algorithms can construct index trees that can minimize index probe costs in wireless mobile computing environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to construct index trees to minimize the average cost incurred in broadcasting data over wireless channels.
the design and analysis of data indexing for wireless data broadcasting.
the problem of designing index trees for sequential broadcasting in order to minimize the average cost incurred in index probes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods can significantly reduce the cost of index probing and, thus, the energy consumption of wireless data broadcasting.
the use of indexed sequential data broadcasting in mobile computing is a promising technique for energy savings.

, for the case where the index fanout can vary, the optimal index tree is the one that is designed in such a way that the access skew of the data records is reflected in the fanouts of the index tree nodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cost of data broadcast can be minimized by employing an im balanced index tree that is constructed based on the skewed data access.
we propose an effective way to organize data with skewed access frequencies to achieve energy saving in wireless mobile computing.
the index trees we propose are more efficient than the existing methods, and the proposed index tree construction algorithms are efficient and can be used in wireless mobile computing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data indexing can be a powerful tool to achieve energy saving for data broadcasting in wireless computing.
the use of variant index fanouts can significantly reduce the cost of index probe in sequential broadcast.
the cost of data broadcast can be reduced by employing a data organization with an imbalanced index structure that is constructed in accordance with data record access skew.
